subtitle: When Nalanda Spoke to the Sea

panels.shot: split composition, half showing a regal court in Bengal, half a distant island shore with ships, joined by a glowing copper plate at the center
panels.action: Devapala & Balaputradeva stand on opposite halves of the frame, each in his own courtly setting, their hands almost touching the same suspended copper plate that gleams between Bengal's palaces and a Sumatran coastline with sailing vessels.

dialogue.text: In Devapala’s thirty-third year, a king from the sea wrote to Nalanda—binding Bengal to Sumatra with five villages and a single copper plate.

i18n.hi: देवपाल के तैंतीसवें वर्ष में, सागर का एक राजा नालंदा को लिखता है—पाँच गाँव और एक ताम्रपत्र से बंगाल को सुमात्रा से बाँध देता है।

panels.shot: wide aerial over the eastern Indian subcontinent, slow drift from Bengal’s rivers to the Bay of Bengal and beyond
panels.action: The Ganga and its eastern branches shimmer beneath monsoon clouds, widening into the Bay of Bengal, where faint silhouettes of ships mark distant routes toward unseen islands.

dialogue.text: By the ninth century, Bengal’s rivers did not end at the sea. They flowed into a wide world of winds, ships and islands that Indian texts called Suvarnadvipa—the Island of Gold.

i18n.hi: नौवीं सदी तक, बंगाल की नदियाँ सागर पर नहीं रुकतीं। वे हवाओं, जहाज़ों और द्वीपों की उस दुनिया में उतरती हैं जिसे भारतीय ग्रंथ सुवर्णद्वीप—सोने का द्वीप—कहते थे।

panels.shot: medium close on Devapala’s half of the character sheet, courtly low-angle, with faint overlay of armies and temples behind him
panels.action: Devapala stands in a royal hall with carved pillars and lotus motifs, a map-scroll at his side and courtiers in the shadows, his face calm yet alert as if weighing power and piety together.

dialogue.text: In this age, Devapala of the Pala line ruled from Bengal and Bihar, famed in inscriptions as a powerful protector of the dharma and patron of monasteries like Nalanda.

i18n.hi: यही समय था, जब पाल वंश के देवपाल बंगाल और बिहार से राज करते थे—शिलालेखों में धर्म के शक्तिशाली रक्षक, और नालंदा जैसे मठों के बड़े संरक्षक।

panels.shot: medium on Balaputradeva’s half of the character sheet, seated on an island throne with sea beyond, three-quarter profile
panels.action: Balaputradeva sits on a wooden throne carved with lotus and naga motifs, open to a veranda where the sea and moored ships stretch behind him, counselors standing respectfully at a distance.

dialogue.text: Across the Bay, in Suvarnadvipa, Balaputradeva of the Sailendra house held an island realm, shaped by both local seas and long memories of Indian teachers and texts.

i18n.hi: उधर खाड़ी के पार सुवर्णद्वीप में, शैलेन्द्र कुल के बलपुत्रदेव समुद्रों से घिरे द्वीप राज्य पर शासन करते थे—जहाँ स्थानीय लहरें और भारतीय आचार्य‑ग्रंथों की पुरानी यादें, दोनों बसती थीं।

panels.shot: intercut close-ups: Devapala studying a palm-leaf manuscript, Balaputradeva gazing at a bronze Buddha; both lit by lamplight
panels.action: On one side Devapala leans over a palm-leaf charter with a monk beside him; on the other, Balaputradeva’s hand rests near a bronze Buddha image as he listens to a visiting monk or scholar.

dialogue.text: Both courts heard of Nalanda, the great monastery in Bihar, where monks from many lands studied logic, grammar and the Buddha’s path under Pala protection.

i18n.hi: दोनों दरबारों तक ख्याति पहुँची नालंदा की—बिहार का महान विद्यापीठ, जहाँ अनेक देशों के भिक्षु पालों की छत्रछाया में तर्क, व्याकरण और बुद्ध का मार्ग सीखते थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of Nalanda’s red-brick complex, slightly elevated, monks moving through corridors
panels.action: The expansive red-brick towers and courtyards of Nalanda rise under a clear sky, monks in saffron and red robes crossing its corridors, with nearby village fields stretching toward the horizon.

dialogue.text: Nalanda was not just walls of brick. It was a living network of villages and endowments, feeding thousands of monks, copying manuscripts, and drawing students from as far as Southeast Asia.

i18n.hi: नालंदा सिर्फ़ ईंटों की दीवार नहीं थी। यह जीवित जाल था—गाँवों और दानों का—जो हज़ारों भिक्षुओं को खिलाता, ग्रंथों की नकल करवाता, और विद्यार्थियों को दूर दक्षिण‑पूर्व एशिया तक से खींच लाता।

panels.shot: medium interior of Balaputradeva’s council chamber, angled from the side, focus on a monk pointing at a map
panels.action: Balaputradeva listens on his throne as a robed monk gestures to a palm-leaf map showing Nalanda’s name, courtiers leaning in while the open doorway frames the bright sea outside.

dialogue.text: “Mahārāja, let our island support a house of learning at Nalanda,”

i18n.hi: “महाराज, हमारे द्वीप को नालंदा में एक विद्यालाय का भार उठाने दीजिए।”

panels.shot: close-up on Balaputradeva’s thoughtful face, slight downward angle, as he makes a decision
panels.action: Balaputradeva’s face is half in shadow, his eyes narrowed with resolve, one hand tightening on the arm of his throne as if he has chosen a path across the sea.

dialogue.text: Balaputradeva chose not to send warriors or merchants, but a request. He would honor Nalanda, and seek from Devapala a lasting place for his own foundation there.

i18n.hi: बलपुत्रदेव ने सैनिक या व्यापारी नहीं, एक विनती भेजी। वह नालंदा का सम्मान करेंगे, और देवपाल से वहाँ अपनी स्थायी स्थापना के लिए जगह माँगेंगे।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle view from a ship’s deck, crew hauling sails, Balaputradeva’s envoys at the prow
panels.action: A sturdy wooden ship cuts through rolling waves, its sail billowing, as robed envoys bearing sealed letters and gifts stand near the prow, looking toward the distant hazy coastline of eastern India.

dialogue.text: So the sea carried his message. Envoys from Suvarnadvipa crossed the Bay of Bengal, bearing gifts and a petition from a monarch who called himself ‘king of the island realm.’

i18n.hi: सागर ने इस संदेश को ढोया। सुवर्णद्वीप के दूत उपहारों और याचिका के साथ बंगाल की खाड़ी पार करते हैं—उस राजा की ओर से जो खुद को ‘द्वीप‑सम्राट’ कहता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Devapala’s court in Bengal, with envoys arriving, viewed from behind their shoulders toward the throne
panels.action: In Devapala’s pillared hall, local nobles and monks stand aside as sea-weathered envoys bow, extending a casket of gifts and sealed palm-leaf documents toward the richly robed king on his throne.

dialogue.text: “O Devapala, guardian of Nalanda, Balaputradeva of Suvarnadvipa sends greetings,”

i18n.hi: “हे देवपाल, नालंदा के रक्षक, सुवर्णद्वीप के बलपुत्रदेव की ओर से वंदन।”

panels.shot: close on Devapala’s hands unrolling the petition, overhead view of the script lines
panels.action: Devapala’s adorned hands carefully unroll a long strip of palm-leaf, tiny precise letters running line after line as a monk or scribe leans in to read out the request.

dialogue.text: The petition asked that lands be granted near Nalanda, to support a monastery founded by Balaputradeva, in the name of both kings and for the welfare of the sangha.

i18n.hi: याचिका में आग्रह था कि नालंदा के पास भूमि दी जाए—एक मठ के लिए, जिसे बलपुत्रदेव दोनों राजाओं के नाम पर और संघ के कल्याण के लिए बसाना चाहते थे।

panels.shot: medium three-quarter shot of Devapala in consultation with monks and ministers, triangle composition
panels.action: Devapala sits slightly forward on his throne, flanked by a senior monk holding a manuscript and a minister with a land register, all three engaged in quiet but intense discussion.

dialogue.text: “This gift will bind Nalanda to the seas, and our name to theirs,”

i18n.hi: “यह दान नालंदा को सागरों से जोड़ेगा—और हमारे नाम को उनके नाम से।”

panels.shot: close-up of an artisan engraving on a sheet of copper, side-light catching the incised letters
panels.action: A copper plate lies on a low workbench as a craftsman, guided by a scribe, carefully incises curling characters into the glowing metal, each stroke sharp under the lamplight.

dialogue.text: Devapala agreed. In his thirty-third regnal year, a copper plate charter was ordered, naming five villages and confirming the grant for Balaputradeva’s monastery at Nalanda.

i18n.hi: देवपाल मान गए। अपने तैंतीसवें राजवर्ष में उन्होंने ताम्रपत्र खुदवाया—पाँच गाँवों के नाम लिखवाकर, नालंदा में बलपुत्रदेव के मठ के लिए अनुदान पक्का कर दिया।

panels.shot: wide rural shot of Bengal villages, with farmers in fields and a Nalanda monk arriving, slightly raised viewpoint
panels.action: Green fields ripple around clustered huts as a monk from Nalanda, followed by a local official, points out boundary trees and irrigation channels to villagers who pause from their work to watch.

dialogue.text: Those five villages—named line by line in the inscription—were woven into Nalanda’s support. Fields, water, and grain in Bengal would now sustain a Sumatran king’s foundation.

i18n.hi: वे पाँचों गाँव—शिलालेख में पंक्ति‑पंक्ति उकेरे गए—अब नालंदा की आजीविका से जुड़ गए। बंगाल की खेती, जल और अनाज अब सुमात्रा के राजा की स्थापना को भी सँभालेंगे।

panels.shot: interior of a new monastery block at Nalanda, with a discreet Sailendra emblem, monks settling in
panels.action: Within Nalanda’s brick cloisters, a freshly plastered hall bears subtle island-style carvings, as monks unroll palm-leaf manuscripts and arrange simple bedding in cells along a shaded corridor.

dialogue.text: Within Nalanda, a new establishment took shape under Balaputradeva’s name, a Sailendra imprint inside a Pala-guarded university, merging island devotion with Gangetic scholarship.

i18n.hi: नालंदा के भीतर बलपुत्रदेव के नाम का नया प्रतिष्ठान खड़ा हुआ—शैलेन्द्र की छाप, पालों से सुरक्षित विश्वविद्यालय के बीच—जहाँ द्वीप की भक्ति गंगातटी विद्या से घुल गयी।

panels.shot: symbolic split-panel: present-day archaeology overlaid with ghostly image of Devapala and Balaputradeva standing behind the copper plate
panels.action: Broken bricks, excavated foundations and a displayed copper plate in a modern museum case occupy the foreground, while faint spectral figures of Devapala and Balaputradeva stand behind, hands resting near where the inscription lies.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, Nalanda’s ruins lay silent. But when the copper plate was found and read, it spoke again of that day when two distant kings shared one monastery in ink and metal.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीतीं, नालंदा खंडहर हो गया। पर जब वह ताम्रपत्र मिला और पढ़ा गया, उसने फिर कहानियाँ सुनाईं—उस दिन की, जब दो दूरस्थ राजाओं ने एक ही मठ को स्याही और धातु से साझा किया था।

panels.shot: medium shot of a modern scholar in a library or study, reading a facsimile of the inscription, maps of the Bay of Bengal on the wall
panels.action: A scholar sits at a desk, tracing lines on a facsimile of the Devapala copper plate while a large map of the Bay of Bengal, marked with routes between Bengal and Sumatra, hangs behind.

dialogue.text: For historians, this is not a tale of conquest or trade tribute. It is clear, epigraphic proof that Pala Bengal stood inside a Buddhist world reaching across the Bay to the Sailendra islands.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकारों के लिए यह न विजय की कथा है, न कर‑व्यापार की। यह साफ़, शिलालेखी प्रमाण है कि पालकालीन बंगाल एक ऐसे बौद्ध जगत के भीतर था जो खाड़ी पार शैलेन्द्र द्वीपों तक फैला था।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the copper plate itself, displayed against a dark background, letters crisp and highlighted
panels.action: The Nalanda copper plate rests alone against a velvet backdrop, its engraved characters catching the light, the edges worn yet intact, every line a bridge between land, sea and memory.

dialogue.text: On this single sheet of copper, Devapala’s name, Balaputradeva’s title, and five village names fix a moment when learning made Bengal and Sumatra neighbors without a sword being drawn.

i18n.hi: इसी एक ताम्रपत्र पर देवपाल का नाम, बलपुत्रदेव की उपाधि और पाँच गाँवों की सूची उस पल को जड़ देती है—जब विद्या ने बंगाल और सुमात्रा को बिना तलवार निकाले पड़ोसी बना दिया।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot: stylized Bay of Bengal at dusk, faint outlines of Nalanda and a Sumatran shrine on opposite horizons, linked by a glowing script line
panels.action: At dusk, the calm Bay of Bengal stretches between two distant horizons—on one side the silhouette of Nalanda’s towers, on the other an island shrine—joined by a faint, luminous line shaped like flowing script.

dialogue.text: The copper plate of Devapala and Balaputradeva reminds us that empires fade, but when a king uses his power to endow learning, even an ocean can become a quiet corridor between minds.

i18n.hi: देवपाल‑बलपुत्रदेव का यह ताम्रपत्र याद दिलाता है—साम्राज्य ढह जाते हैं, पर जब राजा अपनी शक्ति विद्या को दान करते हैं, तब समंदर भी मनों के बीच एक शांत गलियारा बन सकता है।

title_i18n.hi: देवपाल और सागर से आया राजा

subtitle_i18n.en: When Nalanda Spoke to the Sea
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब नालंदा ने सागर से बात की
